title: In a double complex with exact rows a cycle of the row-cokernel complex lifts to a zig-zag
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A=(A_{p,q},d,\delta)_{p,q\ge0}$ be a homological double complex of $R$-modules: $R$-modules $A_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge0$) and $R$-linear maps $d_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p-1,q}$ ($p\ge1$) and $\delta_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p,q-1}$ ($q\ge1$) with $d_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=0$, $\delta_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}=0$ and $\delta_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ whenever defined; put $A_{p,q}=0$ if $p<0$ or $q<0$ and let $d_{0,q}$, $\delta_{p,0}$ and all maps out of or into a zero module be $0$. A morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of such double complexes is a family of $R$-linear maps $\Phi_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{p,q}$ with $\Phi d=d\Phi$ and $\Phi\delta=\delta\Phi$. Let $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,q}:A_{1,q}\to A_{0,q})$ with projection $\pi_q:A_{0,q}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ ($q\ge0$); since $\delta_{0,q}(\operatorname{im}d_{1,q})=d_{1,q-1}(\delta_{1,q}(A_{1,q}))\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{1,q-1}$, the map $\delta_{0,q}$ induces $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}$ with $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}$ ($q\ge1$), and $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ is a chain complex of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; a morphism $\Phi$ induces the morphism of complexes $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$ with $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$. Assume that every row of $A$ is exact in positive degrees: for all $q\ge0$ and $p\ge1$ the sequence $A_{p+1,q}\xrightarrow{d_{p+1,q}}A_{p,q}\xrightarrow{d_{p,q}}A_{p-1,q}$ is exact at $A_{p,q}$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Let $Z_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{p,q}$ and $B_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)$ be the modules of zig-zags and of trivial zig-zags of total degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Then for every $n\ge0$ and every $x\in A_{0,n}$ such that $\pi_n(x)$ is a cycle of $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ (that is, $n=0$ or $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(x))=0$) there is a zig-zag $a\in Z_n(A)$ with $a_{0,n}=x$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), tag verified in tags/tags (00M1,algebra-lemma-no-spectral-sequence); proof, lines 18464-18481: 'First we show that these maps are surjective. ... And so on until a full zig-zag is found.'

proof.text: Case $n=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], $T_0(A)=A_{0,0}$ and the defining conditions of $Z_0(A)$ are empty (there is no $p\ge1$ with $p+q=0$, $q\ge0$), so $Z_0(A)=A_{0,0}$; the element $a=x$ is a zig-zag with $a_{0,0}=x$. From now on $n\ge1$, and then the hypothesis says $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(x))=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18464-18481 ('First we show that these maps are surjective ... And so on until a full zig-zag is found.')

proof.text: Inductive claim. For $0\le k\le n$ let $C(k)$ be the assertion: there are elements $a_{j,n-j}\in A_{j,n-j}$ for $0\le j\le k$ with $a_{0,n}=x$ and $d_{j,n-j}(a_{j,n-j})=\delta_{j-1,n-j+1}(a_{j-1,n-j+1})$ for every $1\le j\le k$. We prove $C(n)$ by induction on $k$: $C(0)$ holds with $a_{0,n}:=x$ (no condition to check); step 3 proves $C(0)\Rightarrow C(1)$ and step 4 proves $C(k-1)\Rightarrow C(k)$ for $2\le k\le n$, each time keeping the elements already chosen and choosing one new element $a_{k,n-k}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18464-18481 ('First we show that these maps are surjective ... And so on until a full zig-zag is found.')

proof.text: $C(0)\Rightarrow C(1)$ (the source: 'Because $\delta(r)=0$, we see that $\delta(a_{0,i})$ is in the image of $d$'). By the definition of $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$ in the statement, $\pi_{n-1}(\delta_{0,n}(x))=\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n(\pi_n(x))=0$ (here $n\ge1$, so $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$ is defined and the cycle condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] is this equation). The kernel of the projection $\pi_{n-1}:A_{0,n-1}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n-1}=A_{0,n-1}/d_{1,n-1}(A_{1,n-1})$ is $d_{1,n-1}(A_{1,n-1})$, so there is $a_{1,n-1}\in A_{1,n-1}$ with $d_{1,n-1}(a_{1,n-1})=\delta_{0,n}(a_{0,n})$. Together with $a_{0,n}=x$ this is $C(1)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18464-18481 ('First we show that these maps are surjective ... And so on until a full zig-zag is found.')

proof.text: $C(k-1)\Rightarrow C(k)$ for $2\le k\le n$ (the source: 'This in turn implies that $\delta(a_{1,i-1})$ is in the kernel of $d$ ... By exactness of the rows we find an element $a_{2,i-2}$ ... And so on'). Given $a_{0,n},\dots,a_{k-1,n-k+1}$ as in $C(k-1)$, put $y=\delta_{k-1,n-k+1}(a_{k-1,n-k+1})\in A_{k-1,n-k}$ (defined since $n-k+1\ge1$). Using the commutation $d_{k-1,n-k}\circ\delta_{k-1,n-k+1}=\delta_{k-2,n-k+1}\circ d_{k-1,n-k+1}$ (an instance of $\delta_{p-1,q}d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\delta_{p,q}$ with $(p,q)=(k-1,n-k+1)$, $p\ge1$, $q\ge1$), the relation of $C(k-1)$ for $j=k-1$, namely $d_{k-1,n-k+1}(a_{k-1,n-k+1})=\delta_{k-2,n-k+2}(a_{k-2,n-k+2})$, and $\delta_{k-2,n-k+1}\circ\delta_{k-2,n-k+2}=0$, we get $d_{k-1,n-k}(y)=\delta_{k-2,n-k+1}(\delta_{k-2,n-k+2}(a_{k-2,n-k+2}))=0$. Since $p:=k-1\ge1$ and $q:=n-k\ge0$, the hypothesis says that the row $A_{k,n-k}\xrightarrow{d_{k,n-k}}A_{k-1,n-k}\xrightarrow{d_{k-1,n-k}}A_{k-2,n-k}$ is exact at $A_{k-1,n-k}$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]; in the category of $R$-modules the image and kernel subobjects are the submodules $d_{k,n-k}(A_{k,n-k})$ and $\ker d_{k-1,n-k}$, so these are equal and $y\in d_{k,n-k}(A_{k,n-k})$. Choose $a_{k,n-k}\in A_{k,n-k}$ with $d_{k,n-k}(a_{k,n-k})=y=\delta_{k-1,n-k+1}(a_{k-1,n-k+1})$; this is the relation for $j=k$, so $C(k)$ holds.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18464-18481 ('First we show that these maps are surjective ... And so on until a full zig-zag is found.')

proof.text: Conclusion ('until a full zig-zag is found'). By steps 2-4, $C(n)$ holds: we have $a=(a_{n,0},a_{n-1,1},\dots,a_{0,n})\in T_n(A)$ with $a_{0,n}=x$ and $d_{j,n-j}(a_{j,n-j})=\delta_{j-1,n-j+1}(a_{j-1,n-j+1})$ for $1\le j\le n$. Writing $(p,q)=(j,n-j)$, these are exactly the conditions $d_{p,q}(a_{p,q})=\delta_{p-1,q+1}(a_{p-1,q+1})$ for all $p\ge1$, $q\ge0$, $p+q=n$ defining $Z_n(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module], so $a\in Z_n(A)$ and $a_{0,n}=x$.

lean.statement: theorem row_cycle_lifts_to_zigzag (A : HomologicalComplex₂ (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.down ℕ) (ComplexShape.down ℕ)) (hrow : ∀ (p q : ℕ), 0 < p → (ShortComplex.mk ((A.d (p + 1) p).f q) ((A.d p (p - 1)).f q) (by rw [← HomologicalComplex.comp_f, A.d_comp_d, HomologicalComplex.zero_f])).Exact) (n : ℕ) (x : (A.X 0).X n) (hcycle : ∃ c : (A.opcycles 0).cycles n, (A.opcycles 0).iCycles n c = (A.pOpcycles 0).f n x) : ∃ a : zigzagTotal A n, a ∈ zigzagCycles A n ∧ DirectSum.component R (ZigzagIndex n) (fun i : ZigzagIndex n => (A.X i.1.1).X i.1.2) ⟨(0, n), by omega⟩ a = x

reviewed_lean.note: R CommRing; A HomologicalComplex₂ ModuleCat down ℕ x down ℕ (first quadrant, commuting squares); hrow ShortComplex.Exact at every q, p≥1 (not p=0); n, x ∈ A_{0,n}; π_n x cycle of A^rt = A.opcycles 0 via iCycles/pOpcycles (n=0 automatic); conclusion ∃ a ∈ zigzagCycles with (0,n) component x, recorded zigzagTotal/ZigzagIndex
